| Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. | 40 | `delete(name)` | - | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie. | 41 | `toString()` | String | Returns a string representation of the cookies. | 42 43 ### Options 44 45 When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported: 46 47 | Option | Type | Description | 48 | ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 49 | `name` | String | Specifies the name of the cookie. | 50 | `value` | String | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie. | 51 | `expires` | Date | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire. | 52 | `maxAge` | Number | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds. | 53 | `domain` | String | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available. | 54 | `path` | String, default: `'/'` | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain. | 55 | `secure` | Boolean | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security. | 56 | `httpOnly` | Boolean | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access. | 57 | `sameSite` | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior. | 58 | `priority` | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's priority | 59 | `partitioned` | Boolean | Indicates whether the cookie is [partitioned](https://github.com/privacycg/CHIPS). | 60 61 The only option with a default value is `path`. 62 63 To learn more about these options, see the [MDN docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies). 64 65 ## Good to know 66 67 - `cookies` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access cookies. 68 - In version 14 and earlier, `cookies` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 69 - `cookies` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in a layout or page will opt a route into [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering). 70 - The `.delete` method can only be called: 71 - In a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 72 - If it belongs to the same domain from which `.set` is called. For wildcard domains, the specific subdomain must be an exact match. Additionally, the code must be executed on the same protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) as the cookie you want to delete. 73 - HTTP does not allow setting cookies after streaming starts, so you must use `.set` in a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 74 75 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Components 76 77 When working with cookies in Server Components, it's important to understand that cookies are fundamentally a client-side storage mechanism: 78 79 - **Reading cookies** works in Server Components because you're accessing the cookie data that the client's browser sends to the server in the HTTP request headers. 80 - **Setting cookies** is not supported during Server Component rendering. To modify cookies, invoke a Server Function from the client or use a Route Handler. 81 82 The server can only send instructions (via `Set-Cookie` headers) to tell the browser to store cookies - the actual storage happens on the client side. This is why cookie operations that modify state (`.set`, `.delete`) must be performed in a Server Function or Route Handler where the response headers can be properly set. 83 84 ## Understanding Cookie Behavior in Server Functions 85 86 After you set or delete a cookie in a Server Function, Next.js can return both the updated UI and new data in a single server roundtrip when the function is used as a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions) (e.g., passed to a form's `action` prop). [`Headers.entries()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/entries): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object. 37 - [`Headers.forEach()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/forEach): Executes a provided function once for each key/value pair in this `Headers` object. 38 - [`Headers.get()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/get): Returns a [`String`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/String) sequence of all the values of a header within a `Headers` object with a given name. 39 - [`Headers.has()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/has): Returns a boolean stating whether a `Headers` object contains a certain header. 40 - [`Headers.keys()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/keys): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 41 - [`Headers.values()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Headers/values): Returns an [`iterator`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Iteration_protocols) allowing you to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object. 42 43 ## Good to know 44 45 - `headers` is an **asynchronous** function that returns a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 46 - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 47 - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. 48 - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function. 46 - In version 14 and earlier, `headers` was a synchronous function. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 47 - Since `headers` is read-only, you cannot `set` or `delete` the outgoing request headers. 48 - `headers` is a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) whose returned values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it in will opt a route into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)**. 49 50 ## Examples 51 52 ### Using the Authorization header 53 54 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" 55 import { headers } from 'next/headers' 56 57 export default async function Page() { 58 const authorization = (await headers()).get('authorization') 59 const res = await fetch('...', { 60 headers: { authorization }, // Forward the authorization header 61 }) 62 const user = await res.json() 63 64 return
